messages:
maria: quick heads up — local sampleapp build behaves fine in node, but when bundled for edge with Vite the runtime crashes. steps to repro below.

maria: repro steps (minimal):
1) git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/sample-app-sdk.git --branch/edge-repro
2) npm ci && npm run build:edge
3) deploy to local edge runtime (we use fast-edge-sim) or run with env EDGE=1 npm start

maria: error seen on edge runtime: "TypeError: createClient is not a function" coming from src/server/api.ts where we do:

  import Redwood from 'redwood-inference';
  const client = Redwood.createClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });

maria: note: the published package has both ESM and CJS entrypoints and a conditional export. Vite's esbuild step seems to flatten the conditional export to a single default import and the edge shim's loader treats it as undefined.

devon: can you paste the built bundle snippet where createClient reference is?

maria: sure — this is from dist/edge/index.js after vite build:

  var r = n('redwood-inference');
  var client = r.createClient({apiKey:process.env.RW_KEY});

maria: but r is actually an object like { default: { createClient: [Function] } } so r.createClient is undefined. In node (CJS) the runtime coerces default, but the edge loader doesn't.

olivia: interesting — we saw something similar when rollup's commonjs plugin inlined default exports. For some builds the bundler rewrites imports to `var r = __toCommonJS(require('redwood-inference'))` and then consumers call r.createClient expecting the flattening.

kevin: does adding `import * as Redwood from 'redwood-inference'` change behavior? that preserves namespace shape more consistently across bundlers.

maria: tried that — with vite it still ends up as default-only in the built file. leaving `type: "module"` in package.json changes some outcomes.

devon: two angles: 1) make our package exports guarantee `createClient` at top-level (add `exports.createClient = module.exports.createClient` shim for CJS build), 2) update sampleapp docs to import named exports e.g. `import { createClient } from 'redwood-inference'` which is safer.

maria: also a typing issue — TS users get: "Namespace 'redwood-inference' Has no exported member 'createClient'" depending on tsconfig.moduleResolution and whether types point at ./dist/types/index.d.ts. Edge-bundled consumers pick the wrong .d.ts because rollup/tsc path mapping breaks.

olivia: can you attach a tiny patch in sampleapp that reproduces with a single command? we should add to devex repro suite.

maria: put a script in the repo: "npm run repro:edge" that runs build + edge-sim and logs. link: https://gist.github.com/maria/edge-repro-snippet (just a gist, not in repo yet)

kevin: CI note — ci-bot: build job #482 failed on the repro branch with the same runtime error.

ci-bot: build failed: /builds/sample-app-sdk/edge-repro — see logs: https://ci.internal/build/482 (exit code 1)

devon: proposal: in our SDK build pipeline produce an additional interop layer file dist/interop.cjs that ensures top-level named exports for common patterns. Also add tests that run the built bundle through esbuild and vite and check shape.

maria: +1. I'll open a small PR to sampleapp to show the workaround and link to SDK PR once we have one. For now, doc the recommended import style for edge: `import { createClient } from 'redwood-inference'` and add note about bundler flags to preserve default/namespace semantics.

olivia: one more gotcha — auth/retry behavior: edge runtime strips Authorization header for internal fetch polyfills in some setups. if createClient uses fetch-based auth refresh, retries silently fail. add a note to sampleapp to set KEEP_AUTH_HEADER=true in edge-sim to replicate.

kevin: thanks — will add a test matrix item: (vite|rollup|webpack) x (node|edge-sim) x (tsc types check) to catch this earlier.

maria: ok I'll add minimal repro and update participants once PRs are open. thanks all. :thumbsup:
